Zharp for .NET: errors with the code that ran, traces, failed queries, request headers and (optionally) logs, sent to Zharp over OpenTelemetry. AddZharp() on any Generic Host, ZharpSdk.Init() anywhere else.

Zharp for classic ASP.NET on .NET Framework (MVC 5, Web API 2, WebForms) on IIS: installs itself (no web.config edit), traces requests by route, reports each failure once with the code that ran, records headers (secrets filtered) and failed queries.

Zharp for ASP.NET Web API 2 on .NET Framework: config.AddZharp() reports what controllers throw — Web API handles it before Application_Error sees it — once, with the code that ran. Brings Zharp.AspNet.

Zharp for ASP.NET Core: builder.Services.AddZharp() traces every request by its route, reports each failure once with the code that ran, records request and response headers (secrets filtered) and failed queries.

Zharp for .NET on AWS Lambda: ZharpLambda.Wrap(handler) traces each invocation (cold starts marked), reports what it throws once with the code that ran, and sends everything before the function freezes.

Zharp's MSBuild step: after a Release build, uploads the project's sources as a source bundle under the build's PDB ID, so Zharp shows the code that ran for builds that don't embed their sources. Reference it with PrivateAssets="all".

Zharp for .NET on Google Cloud Run functions (Cloud Functions): one assembly attribute traces each invocation, reports what the function throws once with the code that ran, and sends everything before the instance is throttled.
